correctness.rationale: Every subgroup outside the finite abelian normal kernel is uniquely K(H,a), where a ranges over cosets A/H; every saturated chain has one index-2 crossing, and the remaining covers are exactly covers of A. This yields the unrestricted count \(\sum_{H\le A}\lvert A:H\rvert b(H)b(A/H)\). For sorted indices, the pivot can occur only at one of the e+1 positions within the initial 2-primary block, with \(\lvert A\rvert/2^j\) distinct coset choices at position j. The geometric sum proves \(F(A)(2\lvert A\rvert-\lvert A_{\mathrm{odd}}\rvert)\). For odd squarefree n, the H=1 term gives at least n k! unrestricted chains and exactly n sorted chains. Exhaustive direct Cayley-table subgroup-lattice enumeration on fifteen small mixed, cyclic, and noncyclic kernels independently reproduced the count (VERIFY_OK). The symbolic cover argument, not these finite checks, proves the universal claim.

value.rationale: The new motivated counting invariant refines the recent existence/nonexistence problem: it gives an exact all-parameter law throughout generalized dihedral groups, including arbitrary finite abelian kernels. The universal factor \(2\lvert A\rvert-\lvert A_{\mathrm{odd}}\rvert\) reveals an invariant two-adic insertion mechanism, and odd squarefree ordinary dihedral groups exhibit a sharp qualitative gap between universal existence and at most \(1/k!\) density among maximal chains. This is a natural complete enumeration and structural lemma, not an arbitrary finite cutoff.
